transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. We need to finalize the production message-streaming platform decision for the customer-notification service before the next integration milestone. The two finalists are KafkaCloud and StreamGrid — both passed our benchmark of 20,000 messages per second with sub-250-millisecond median delivery latency. The draft architecture currently recommends StreamGrid based on simpler operational setup and an initial capacity estimate of four brokers. Before I record a final decision, I'd like to hear from each of you on backend, support engineering, security, and FinOps. Could we go around and get your sign-off perspectives?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. While testing the notification client's retry behavior this morning, I confirmed that the service already has a KafkaCloud-compatible producer and consumer path. That means using KafkaCloud would require only about two days of adapter cleanup, whereas moving to StreamGrid would require a new two-week client integration. I haven't updated the architecture document yet, so the current StreamGrid recommendation doesn't reflect this finding.

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go further. During a customer escalation yesterday, I confirmed that three enterprise customers require notifications for each account to remain in order. KafkaCloud can guarantee that ordering using a customer_id partition key, while StreamGrid's tested mode cannot. I have not yet added this requirement to the review ticket, but it directly impacts the platform choice.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical security concern before we proceed. During a data-flow review this afternoon, I confirmed that notification payloads contain phone numbers and must be stored and processed in eu-central-1. KafkaCloud offers that processing region for this service, while StreamGrid's selected tier does not. I have not yet filed the security architecture note on this, but this is a hard compliance blocker for StreamGrid — phone numbers are PII, and EU data residency requirements mean we cannot use a platform that cannot guarantee processing in eu-central-1.

transcript.text: I need to share a FinOps finding before we proceed. When I reconciled the cloud account this morning, I found that existing KafkaCloud reserved-capacity credits cover exactly six production brokers through the service's first year. StreamGrid has no equivalent credit. The production deployment must provision all six KafkaCloud brokers, setting production_broker_count to exactly 6 to use the full reserved-capacity allocation. I have not yet amended the four-broker estimate in the draft architecture, so that figure doesn't reflect this.

commitments.detail: Update the draft architecture document to replace the StreamGrid recommendation with KafkaCloud, reflecting the four factors raised in this review.
Add the per-account notification ordering requirement to the review ticket, with customer_id as the partition key.
File the security architecture note documenting that notification payloads contain phone numbers (PII) and that KafkaCloud processing in eu-central-1 satisfies EU data residency requirements.
Amend the four-broker estimate to six brokers, reflecting the full KafkaCloud reserved-capacity credit allocation.
Proceed with the approximately two-day KafkaCloud adapter cleanup, leveraging the existing KafkaCloud-compatible producer and consumer path.
